title: Regular precomposition detects smoothness near its image
statement: Let $Z,T,S$ be locally Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $p:Z\to T$ be a regular morphism [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism] and let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose $g\circ p$ is regular. Then there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq T$ containing the set-theoretic image $p(|Z|)$ such that $g|_W:W\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Neither surjectivity nor finite presentation of $p$ is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$, put $t=p(z)$ and $s=g(t)$, and set $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $B=\mathcal O_{T,t}$ and $C=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. The induced local homomorphisms $A\to B\to C$ compose to the stalk map of $g\circ p$, by the composition rule for morphisms of locally ringed spaces. Applying the regular scheme/stalk criterion to $p$ and $g\circ p$ gives regular ring maps $B\to C$ and $A\to C$. In particular $B\to C$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 07R8, lemma-regular; More on Algebra Tag 07C0, lemma-regular-local. Temkin Lemma 2.1.4(ii) uses these local maps.

proof.text: The flat local homomorphism $B\to C$ is faithfully flat and $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is surjective by lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat. Apply lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence to $A\to B\to C$: its composite is regular by Step 1 and its second map is flat and surjective on spectra. Therefore $A\to B$ is regular. This argument is made separately for each chosen $z$, so no surjectivity of $p$ is required.

source.place: Tag 07NT, lemma-regular-permanence; Algebra Tags 00HR and 00HQ, local faithful flatness and spectral surjectivity.

proof.text: The morphism $g$ is locally of finite presentation and its source and target are locally Noetherian. Its stalk map at $t$ is precisely the regular map $A\to B$ from Step 2. Apply lem-per-lfp-regular-stalk-smooth-neighborhood to obtain an open neighborhood of $t$ on which $g$ is smooth. Thus every $t\in p(|Z|)$ has such a neighborhood.

Let $W$ be the union of all open subschemes $U\subseteq T$ for which $g|_U$ is smooth. This is open and contains $p(|Z|)$ by Step 3. Every point of $W$ belongs to such a $U$; the affine smooth charts for $g|_U$ are also charts inside $W$, so $g|_W$ is smooth by the affine-local characterization in def-sbc-smooth-morphisms. If $Z$ is empty, the same construction applies and the image condition is vacuous.
